# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics13100993>
* Supplement (Tables S1-S2, Figures S1-S3): <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/antibiotics13100993/s1>

Kim 2024 gave a single 1 g dose of vancomycin as a 2-h IV infusion to 12
healthy Korean adults, analysed the plasma concentrations by noncompartmental
analysis (NCA) and by population PK, and then used the final population model
in Monte Carlo simulations of intermittent and continuous-infusion regimens
against the steady-state AUC24 target of 400-600 mg h/L. This vignette checks
the packaged model against the paper's NCA and post-hoc summaries (Table 3) and
reproduces the target-attainment simulations (Figures 2-4).

# Population

Twelve healthy volunteers (3 female, 9 male) aged 19-49 years (median 38.5),
height 159-180 cm and weight 53.2-89.4 kg (median 69.5 kg) were enrolled at
Hallym University Sacred Heart Hospital, Anyang, Republic of Korea, between
August 2021 and July 2022 (Kim 2024 Section 2.1 and Table 1). Body surface
area by the DuBois formula had a median of 1.80 m^2 (IQR 1.70-1.92). Renal
function was normal: Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance median 113 mL/min
(IQR 102-124). Plasma was sampled at 2 (end of infusion), 3, 4, 6 and 8 h after
the start of infusion, giving 60 concentrations.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2024_vancomycin"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: two-compartment, zero-order IV infusion | -- | Section 2.2 (OFV 1-/2-/3-cmt), Section 4.4 (ADVAN3 TRANS4) |
| `CL = theta1 * (WT/69.45)^theta2 * (AGE/38.5)^theta3` | -- | Table 2 |
| `V1 = theta4` | -- | Table 2 |
| `Q = theta5 * (WT/69.45)^theta6` | -- | Table 2 |
| `V2 = theta7 * (BSA/1.80)^theta8` | -- | Table 2 |
| `lcl` (theta1) | log(8.83 L/h) | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl` (theta2) | 1.28 | Table 2 |
| `e_age_cl` (theta3) | -0.377 | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (theta4) | log(12.9 L) | Table 2 |
| `lq` (theta5) | log(20.2 L/h) | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_q` (theta6) | 2.38 | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (theta7) | log(27.4 L) | Table 2 |
| `e_bsa_vp` (theta8) | 3.09 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl` | log(0.0798^2 + 1) = 0.006348 | Table 2 (IIV CL 7.98%); exponential IIV model, Section 4.4 |
| `etalvc` | fixed(log(0.474^2 + 1) = 0.2028) | Table 2 (IIV V1 47.4%, fixed); Section 2.2 |
| `propSd` | 0.0694 | Table 2 (proportional error 6.94%) |
| BSA (DuBois) | 0.007184 * HT^0.725 * WT^0.425 | Section 2.1 |

# Virtual cohort

The covariate distributions follow Table 1. Weight is drawn log-normally with
median 69.5 kg and CV 18%, height normally with mean 170 cm and SD 7.1 cm
(CV 4.16%), each truncated to the observed range; age is uniform over the
observed 19-49 years; BSA is computed from height and weight by the DuBois
formula the paper used. Sex is not a model covariate.

```{r cohort-helpers}
# Draw from a distribution truncated to [lo, hi] by inverting its CDF on the
# truncated probability range, so no draws are discarded.
rtruncnorm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  u <- stats::runif(n, stats::pnorm(lo, mean, sd), stats::pnorm(hi, mean, sd))
  stats::qnorm(u, mean, sd)
}
rtrunclnorm <- function(n, median, cv, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(cv^2 + 1))
  exp(rtruncnorm(n, log(median), sdlog, log(lo), log(hi)))
}
bsa_dubois <- function(ht, wt) 0.007184 * ht^0.725 * wt^0.425

make_cohort <- function(n, age_lo, age_hi) {
  ht <- rtruncnorm(n, 170, 7.07, 159, 180)
  wt <- rtrunclnorm(n, 69.5, 0.18, 53.2, 89.4)
  data.frame(
    AGE = stats::runif(n, age_lo, age_hi),
    WT = wt,
    HT = ht,
    BSA = bsa_dubois(ht, wt)
  )
}
```

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20241010)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241010)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- make_cohort(n_sub, 19, 49) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n_sub), treatment = "1 g IV over 2 h")

cohort |>
  summarise(
    across(c(AGE, WT, HT, BSA), list(median = median, min = min, max = max))
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("covariate", "stat"), names_sep = "_") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual-cohort covariates (compare Kim 2024 Table 1).")
```

# Single-dose simulation

The study design is reproduced exactly: 1000 mg infused over 2 h (rate 500
mg/h) into `central`. Observations are on the `central` state, which returns
the plasma concentration `Cc`.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Kim_2024_vancomycin")
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), 2, 3, 4, 6, 8)))

doses <- cohort |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 1000, rate = 500, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
obs <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated plasma concentrations after a single 1 g, 2-h IV infusion (median and 10th-90th percentiles; 200 virtual subjects). The paper's VPC (Figure S2) covers the 0-8 h sampling window."}
sim |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(Cc, 0.1),
    p50 = median(Cc),
    p90 = quantile(Cc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 8, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time after start of infusion (h)", y = "Vancomycin (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA is run on the paper's sampling schedule (0, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 h, with the
pre-dose concentration taken as zero as in Kim 2024 Section 4.2), so the
simulated and published NCA see the same design. `AUClast` is computed over
0-8 h; `Cmax`, `AUCinf` and the terminal half-life over 0-infinity.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8), !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_dose <- doses |>
  mutate(dur = 2) |>
  select(id, time, amt, dur, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = "dur"
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(8, Inf),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against the published NCA

Kim 2024 Table 3 reports the NCA medians; `ncaComparisonTable()` pools the
simulated side by median too.

```{r nca-compare}
published_nca <- data.frame(
  treatment = "1 g IV over 2 h",
  cmax = 20.8,
  auclast = 73.6,
  aucinf.obs = 97.1,
  half.life = 3.58
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L", aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated versus published NCA medians (Kim 2024 Table 3).")
```

The simulated medians agree with the published NCA medians to within the
20% tolerance. The paper's NCA was run on 12 observed profiles, so a
difference of this order is within the sampling noise of a 12-subject median.

# Post-hoc parameter summaries

Table 3 also summarises the individual post-hoc parameters of the 12
participants. The same quantities are computed here from each virtual
subject's parameters: CL and the volumes per kg, `AUCtau = dose/CL`, and the
distribution and elimination half-lives from the two-compartment
micro-constants.

```{r posthoc}
indiv <- sim |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    k10 = cl / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp,
    beta_sum = k10 + k12 + k21,
    alpha = (beta_sum + sqrt(beta_sum^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2,
    beta = (beta_sum - sqrt(beta_sum^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2,
    cl_kg = cl / WT,
    vc_kg = vc / WT,
    vss_kg = (vc + vp) / WT,
    auctau = 1000 / cl,
    thalf_alpha = log(2) / alpha,
    thalf_beta = log(2) / beta
  )

posthoc_cmp <- indiv |>
  summarise(across(c(cl_kg, vc_kg, vss_kg, auctau, thalf_alpha, thalf_beta), median)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "simulated") |>
  left_join(
    data.frame(
      parameter = c("cl_kg", "vc_kg", "vss_kg", "auctau", "thalf_alpha", "thalf_beta"),
      label = c("CL (L/h/kg)", "VC (L/kg)", "Vss (L/kg)", "AUCtau (mg*h/L)", "t1/2 alpha (h)", "t1/2 beta (h)"),
      published = c(0.131, 0.163, 0.593, 111, 0.259, 3.84)
    ),
    by = "parameter"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)

posthoc_cmp |>
  select(label, published, simulated, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = label,
    "Kim 2024 Table 3 median" = published,
    "Simulated median" = simulated,
    "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Median individual parameters versus Kim 2024 Table 3 (population PK rows).")
```

At the reference subject (69.45 kg, 38.5 years, 1.80 m^2) the typical clearance
is exactly theta1, so `AUCtau` for a 1 g dose is `1000 / 8.83 = 113.3`
mg h/L, matching the Table 3 post-hoc mean of 113 mg h/L.

```{r posthoc-check}
typical <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  data.frame(
    id = 1, time = c(0, 1), amt = c(1000, 0), rate = c(500, 0),
    evid = c(1L, 0L), cmt = "central", WT = 69.45, AGE = 38.5, BSA = 1.80
  )
) |>
  as.data.frame()

stopifnot(
  # Closed form: the reference-subject clearance is theta1 exactly.
  abs(typical$cl[1] - 8.83) < 1e-8,
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed theta or exponent shifts the whole cohort.
  abs(posthoc_cmp$pct_diff[posthoc_cmp$parameter == "cl_kg"]) < 10,
  abs(posthoc_cmp$pct_diff[posthoc_cmp$parameter == "vss_kg"]) < 10,
  abs(posthoc_cmp$pct_diff[posthoc_cmp$parameter == "thalf_beta"]) < 10
)
```

# Dosing simulations (Figures 2-4)

Kim 2024 Section 4.6 computes the steady-state AUC24 as daily dose / CL for
virtual subjects in six age groups, for intermittent doses of 10-30 mg/kg every
6, 8 or 12 h and for continuous infusions of 30-70 mg/kg/day. Because the AUC
depends only on the daily dose and CL, every regimen with the same daily dose
gives the same AUC distribution (for example 15 mg/kg q6h, 20 mg/kg q8h, 30
mg/kg q12h and a 60 mg/kg/day continuous infusion), which is visible in the
paper's Figures 2 and 3. The virtual cohort below has 200 subjects per age
group, with age uniform within the group and weight and height drawn as above.

```{r pta-cohort}
age_groups <- data.frame(
  age_group = c("20-24", "25-29", "30-34", "35-39", "40-44", "45-49"),
  lo = c(20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45)
)
n_per_group <- 200
pta_cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(age_groups)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(n_per_group, age_groups$lo[i], age_groups$lo[i] + 5) |>
    mutate(age_group = age_groups$age_group[i])
})) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))

# Individual CL from the model with IIV: a one-row solve per subject returns
# the algebraic `cl`.
pta_ev <- pta_cohort |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
pta_cl <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, pta_ev, keep = "age_group") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, age_group, WT, cl)
```

```{r pta, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Kim 2024 (and, by daily-dose equivalence, Figure 2): probability that the steady-state AUC24 is at least 400 mg h/L, by age group and daily dose."}
daily_doses <- c(30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 120)
pta <- pta_cl |>
  tidyr::crossing(daily_mgkg = daily_doses) |>
  mutate(auc24 = daily_mgkg * WT / cl) |>
  group_by(age_group, daily_mgkg) |>
  summarise(
    pta = 100 * mean(auc24 >= 400),
    pct_tox = 100 * sum(auc24 > 600) / max(sum(auc24 >= 400), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pta |>
  filter(daily_mgkg <= 70) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_group, pta, colour = factor(daily_mgkg), group = factor(daily_mgkg))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Target attainment (%)", colour = "Daily dose (mg/kg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The table puts the simulated PTA beside the values printed in Kim 2024 Figure
3 (continuous infusion) for the 50 and 60 mg/kg/day rows, which carry the
age gradient, and the toxicity percentage (AUC24 > 600 among those with
AUC24 >= 400) for 70 mg/kg/day.

```{r pta-compare}
published_pta <- data.frame(
  age_group = rep(c("20-24", "25-29", "30-34", "35-39", "40-44", "45-49"), 3),
  quantity = rep(c("PTA, 50 mg/kg/day", "PTA, 60 mg/kg/day", "% AUC > 600, 70 mg/kg/day"), each = 6),
  published = c(
    1, 8, 21, 38, 60, 83,
    41, 72, 87, 95, 100, 100,
    0, 2, 6, 14, 31, 51
  )
)
sim_pta <- bind_rows(
  pta |> filter(daily_mgkg == 50) |> transmute(age_group, quantity = "PTA, 50 mg/kg/day", simulated = pta),
  pta |> filter(daily_mgkg == 60) |> transmute(age_group, quantity = "PTA, 60 mg/kg/day", simulated = pta),
  pta |> filter(daily_mgkg == 70) |> transmute(age_group, quantity = "% AUC > 600, 70 mg/kg/day", simulated = pct_tox)
)
published_pta |>
  left_join(sim_pta, by = c("age_group", "quantity")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(published, simulated), names_to = "source") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = age_group, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Source" = source) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Target attainment (%) by age group: Kim 2024 Figure 3 versus this simulation.")
```

The simulation reproduces the paper's pattern: PTA rises steeply with age at a
fixed mg/kg dose, because clearance falls with age (exponent -0.377) while the
small IIV on CL (7.98% CV) and the weak net weight dependence of the AUC
(`WT^(1 - 1.28)`) leave little between-subject spread. The age gradient in
the simulation is close to the published one; the exact percentages depend on
the weight and age distributions within each group, which the paper describes
only as "log-normally distributed random variables across a demographic
range".

## AUC versus trough (Figure 4)

Figure 4 relates the steady-state AUC24 to the trough concentration for the
intermittent regimens. The model is linear, so each subject is solved once per
dosing interval at 10 mg/kg and the trough and AUC are scaled to the other
doses. The paper does not state the infusion duration used for the intermittent
regimens; 1 h is assumed here.

```{r trough}
trough_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(c(6, 8, 12), function(tau) {
  base <- pta_cohort |>
    mutate(id = id + 10000 * tau, tau = tau)
  bind_rows(
    base |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 10 * WT, rate = 10 * WT, ii = tau, ss = 1L, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
    base |> mutate(time = tau, amt = 0, rate = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0L, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  )
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

trough_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, trough_ev, keep = c("age_group", "tau")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(time == tau) |>
  mutate(auc24_10 = 10 * WT * (24 / tau) / cl, trough_10 = Cc)

trough_all <- trough_sim |>
  tidyr::crossing(dose_mgkg = c(10, 15, 20, 25, 30)) |>
  mutate(
    auc24 = auc24_10 * dose_mgkg / 10,
    trough = trough_10 * dose_mgkg / 10,
    interval = paste0("q", tau, "h")
  )
```

```{r trough-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Kim 2024: steady-state AUC24 versus trough concentration for intermittent dosing (1-h infusion assumed)."}
ggplot(trough_all, aes(trough, auc24, colour = factor(dose_mgkg))) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 15, xmax = 20, ymin = 400, ymax = 600, fill = NA, colour = "black") +
  facet_grid(interval ~ age_group) +
  labs(x = "Trough concentration (mg/L)", y = "AUC24 (mg*h/L)", colour = "Dose (mg/kg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r trough-slopes}
trough_all |>
  group_by(interval, age_group) |>
  summarise(slope = unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(auc24 ~ trough))[2]), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = age_group, values_from = slope) |>
  dplyr::rename("Interval" = interval) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Slope of AUC24 on trough (mg h/L per mg/L). Kim 2024 Figure 4 prints slopes of 29-31 (q6h), 35-38 (q8h) and 47-55 (q12h).")
```

The qualitative finding of the paper is reproduced: on q6h and q8h dosing a
trough of 15-20 mg/L corresponds to an AUC24 above 600 mg h/L, while q12h
regimens reach AUC24 >= 400 mg h/L at troughs below 15 mg/L. The simulated
slopes are, however, roughly 40-50% steeper than the slopes printed in Figure
4 (the simulated troughs are lower for a given AUC24), and the printed
intercepts (96-150 mg h/L) are higher than the simulated ones. Varying the
assumed infusion duration from 0.5 to 3 h changes the simulated slopes by less
than 15%, so the infusion duration does not account for the gap. The paper does
not report the remaining settings of the Figure 4 simulation (the covariate
distributions, and how the trough was computed), so the difference is recorded
here rather than resolved. The AUC24-based target attainment of Figures 2 and
3, which does not involve the trough, is reproduced closely (table above).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as a percentage without stating whether it
  is a CV or `sqrt(omega^2)`. It is converted with `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`.
  For CL (7.98%) the two readings agree to four digits; for the fixed V1 IIV
  (47.4%) they give 0.203 versus 0.225.
* **IIV on Q and V2.** Section 2.2 says the IIV on Q and V2 fell "to nearly 0"
  once weight and BSA entered the model, and Table 2 lists no IIV for either,
  so neither parameter carries an eta.
* **Virtual-cohort covariates.** The paper gives Table 1 summaries only. Weight
  is drawn log-normally (median 69.5 kg, CV 18%), height normally (mean 170 cm,
  SD 7.1 cm), both truncated to the observed range, and BSA is computed by the
  DuBois formula. For the age-group simulations, age is uniform within each
  5-year group. The paper describes its simulation covariates only as
  log-normally distributed "across a demographic range".
* **Cohort size.** The paper simulated 2000 subjects (intermittent) and 1000
  subjects (continuous); 200 per age group are used here.
* **Intermittent infusion duration.** Not stated for Figure 4; 1 h is assumed.
  The AUC values (Figures 2-3) do not depend on it; the troughs do.
* **Table 3 labels.** The `Clast` and `Tlast` rows of Table 3 carry swapped
  units (`Clast` in h, `Tlast` in mg/L); from the values (Tlast about 8 h,
  matching the last sampling time) the labels, not the numbers, are swapped.
  Neither row is used here.
* **Table S1 title.** The supplement titles the base-model table "meropenem";
  the values are the vancomycin base model described in Section 2.2.
